parole.testo: Borrowed from Caló calé, plural of caló, from Romani kalo, from Sanskrit काल (kāla, “dark, black”). The term originally referred to "dark" copper coins in contrast to "light" silver coins, which were called parné, from parnó (“white”).

parole.significato: to croak, to snuff it (to die)
parole.testo: From Caló diñar (“give”), ultimately from Romani del (“to give”).
